ResearchProjectDef.label: immortal's spear
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A long spear with a leaf blade at one end and a silver pomegranate at the other, the weapon of the royal guard.
Requires 5 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: silk kaftan
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Cut the long open coat of the court, lined, embroidered and belted with a sash.
Requires 5 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: paradise garden
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Wall a square of ground, split it in four with water channels and plant it with roses, cypress and fruit trees. The old word for it was paradise.
Requires 5 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: recurve bow
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A short recurve bow carried in a combined case with its arrows, light enough to shoot from the saddle.
Requires 5 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: saffron pilaf
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Rice steamed with saffron, barberries and butter until the bottom turns to a golden crust, the best part.
Requires 5 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: culture of gardens
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Every house has a courtyard, every courtyard a pool and every pool a bench beside it. Parsians go into the garden to cool their tempers.
Tradition: The mental break threshold of colonists drops by 3%.
Requires 15 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: law of the satraps
ResearchProjectDef.description:
One law for every province, written down, read aloud in the market and enforced by the satrap's own men. People know where they stand.
Tradition: Colonists make arrests 15% more successfully and negotiate 5% better.
Requires 15 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: royal post
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A station every day's ride, a fresh horse in every station and a rider who does not stop for snow, rain, heat or night.
Tradition: Caravans travel 10% faster and colonists get 5% better trade prices.
Requires 20 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: qanats
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Tunnels dug from the foot of the mountains to bring cold, clean water to every village without losing a drop to the sun.
Tradition: Colonists gain immunity 6% faster.
Requires 20 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: akinakes
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Forge the short straight sword of the guard, worn on the right hip in a gold-capped scabbard.
Requires 10 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: carpet loom
ResearchProjectDef.description:
An upright loom, a hundred colours of wool and a pattern held in the weaver's head. A good carpet takes a season and outlives its maker.
Requires 15 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: polo
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Riders, mallets and a wooden ball on a long field. The princes play it to learn horsemanship, and the horses learn too.
Tradition: Colonists train and tame animals 10% more successfully.
Requires 25 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: the Immortals
ResearchProjectDef.description:
The scale coat and the winged helmet of the royal guard. Their number never drops: when one falls, another steps into the empty place.
Requires 25 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: ears of the king
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Officials who travel the provinces, listen to everyone and report only to the court. Envoys of Pars always know whom they are talking to.
Tradition: Colonists negotiate 8% better and have 4% more social impact.
Requires 25 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: the ten thousand
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Drill until the line holds by itself. A wounded guard holds the line until the one behind can take the place.
Tradition: Colonists withstand 5% more pain and hit 1 point more often in melee.
Requires 35 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: jezail
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A long-barrelled flintlock with a sharply curved stock, inlaid with bone and brass. Mountain shots swear by it.
Requires 35 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: grand bazaar
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A covered street of a thousand shops, its guilds, its money changers and its tea houses. Everything has a price and everyone knows it.
Tradition: Colonists get 4% better trade prices and negotiate 3% better.
Requires 45 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: road of kings
ResearchProjectDef.description:
With the western road open again, Parsian caravans move like the post and Parsian envoys are welcome everywhere.
Tradition: Caravans travel 8% faster, and colonists negotiate 5% better and have 5% more social impact.
Requires 50 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.
Unlocked by finishing the nation's story.

ResearchProjectDef.label: naft thrower
ResearchProjectDef.description:
The kings' engineers learn to pump naft through a bronze pipe and light it at the mouth.
Requires 40 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Persian steam army
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Cartridges, rifled barrels and a uniform: the army Pars raised when the factories came.
Outside your heritage, this can be researched only once Pars has reached the Age of Steam.
Requires 45 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Persian electric army
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Machine-made arms, a steel helmet and a field uniform in drab: the army Pars raised when the wires came.
Outside your heritage, this can be researched only once Pars has reached the Electric Age.
Requires 60 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Persian works
ResearchProjectDef.description:
The first electric works of Pars: one machine the nation is proud of, built to its own taste.
Outside your heritage, this can be researched only once Pars has reached the Electric Age.
Requires 50 Parsian knowledge unless this is your heritage.
